headline: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman meets multiple world leaders and top officials at UN General Assembly in New York
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman engaged in discussions on trade, investment, and bilateral cooperation with leaders from over ten countries and international organizations. His visit to New York is for the 81st UN General Assembly session.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a series of high-level meetings with heads of government and top officials of international organizations during his visit to New York. These discussions focused on expanding trade, investment, and bilateral cooperation.
The Prime Minister is in New York to participate in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. He is utilizing the sidelines of the session to engage with leaders from various nations.

On Thursday, PM Rahman met with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul at UN Headquarters, where they discussed strengthening bilateral relations. Later that afternoon, he held talks with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, addressing global and regional issues.

Friday morning saw a meeting with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, covering mutual interests and the regional situation. Earlier in the week, on Wednesday, PM Rahman met Croatian counterpart Andrej Plenkovic to explore trade and investment expansion.

He also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at the Hyatt Grand Central New York hotel. On Tuesday, discussions were held with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to expand cooperation in economy, trade, and investment.

Further diplomatic engagements included a meeting with Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé to discuss bilateral relations and cooperation. Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay and Maldives Vice President Hussain Mohamed Latheef also met PM Rahman.

Other prominent figures who met the Prime Minister included UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) Barham Salih and World Bank President Ajay Banga, highlighting the breadth of his diplomatic outreach.

headline: 10 Sunnahs from Prophet Muhammad's life offer timeless lessons for marital love and harmony
summary: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), despite his busy life, demonstrated profound affection and care, setting an exemplary standard for spouses worldwide. His actions and words reveal a path to a blessed marital bond.
details: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was not only a prophet, statesman, and social reformer but also a loving husband who taught how to nurture delicate emotions and love in marriage through his daily conduct. He stated, "The best of you is he who is best to his wife, and I am the best of you to my wives."

Many men believe hiding affection is a sign of masculinity, but the Prophet (PBUH) was open in expressing his love. When asked who was most beloved to him, he unhesitatingly replied, "Aisha," and among men, "her father (Abu Bakr)."

This expression of love wasn't limited to words but extended to daily habits. Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) would drink from the same spot on a vessel where she had drunk, even when she was menstruating, showing deep respect and closeness.
Small acts of care bring immense blessings in marital life. The Prophet (PBUH) taught that even a morsel of food lovingly placed in a wife's mouth is a source of great reward from Allah.

To keep his wife happy, the Prophet (PBUH) engaged in playful activities and exercise. Aisha (RA) recounted a race where she initially won, and later, after she gained weight, he won, playfully remarking it was "revenge for that previous victory."

While it's common to look presentable outside, maintaining a tidy appearance for one's spouse at home is a sign of marital respect. Aisha (RA) mentioned that upon entering his home, the Prophet (PBUH) would first use a miswak (tooth-cleaning twig).

Finding rest and comfort in a wife's company during moments of fatigue brings great peace to marriage. Aisha (RA) narrated that the Prophet (PBUH) would recline with his head in her lap and recite the Holy Quran, even when she was menstruating.

This practice challenged the pre-Islamic superstition that women were impure during menstruation, showing his profound love and closeness during such times. Another example of deep marital intimacy was spouses bathing together from the same vessel.

The Prophet (PBUH) also supported and entertained his wife. On an Eid day, when a group of Abyssinian youths performed a spear and shield demonstration, he stood and shielded Aisha (RA) with his cloak so she could watch comfortably until she tired.

Even many years after the passing of his first wife, Khadijah (RA), the Prophet (PBUH) would remember her love and contributions with great respect. He would send portions of slaughtered meat to Khadijah's friends, showing his enduring affection.

Many men consider helping with household chores to be against masculinity, but the Prophet (PBUH) broke this false pride. Aisha (RA) stated that he would engage in household tasks like mending his clothes and shoes, and cleaning, until prayer time.
Calling one's wife by beloved and affectionate names is also part of the Sunnah, bringing joy to her heart.
